Here is the COMPLETE picture of what happens on `POST /api/owners`, in execution order.

## Endpoint mapping

The path is assembled from three layers:
- `OwnerRestControllerV1` is annotated `@RequestMapping("/api")` (class level) — `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/controller/v1/OwnerRestControllerV1.java:53`
- It `implements OwnersApi` (OpenAPI-generated interface), which declares `String PATH_ADD_OWNER = "/owners";` and maps `addOwner` with `@RequestMapping(method = RequestMethod.POST, value = "/owners", produces = "application/json", consumes = "application/json")` — `/home/daniel/sandbox/target/generated-sources/openapi/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/api/OwnersApi.java:52`, `:79-87`

Net effect: `POST /api/owners`, consuming/producing JSON, request body `OwnerFieldsDto`.

## 1. The controller method

`OwnerRestControllerV1.addOwner` — `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/controller/v1/OwnerRestControllerV1.java:99-109`

```java
@PreAuthorize("hasRole(@roles.OWNER_ADMIN)")
@Override
public ResponseEntity<OwnerDto> addOwner(OwnerFieldsDto ownerFieldsDto) {
    HttpHeaders headers = new HttpHeaders();
    Owner owner = ownerMapper.toOwner(ownerFieldsDto);
    this.clinicService.saveOwner(owner);
    OwnerDto ownerDto = ownerMapper.toOwnerDto(owner);
    headers.setLocation(UriComponentsBuilder.newInstance()
        .path("/api/owners/{id}").buildAndExpand(owner.getId()).toUri());
    return new ResponseEntity<>(ownerDto, headers, HttpStatus.CREATED);
}
```

The interface's default `addOwner` (OwnersApi.java:85-109) is overridden, so the stub returning `501 NOT_IMPLEMENTED` never runs. On success it returns `201 CREATED` with a `Location: /api/owners/{id}` header.

Note the parameter itself carries the validation trigger. In the interface signature the body is declared `@Valid @RequestBody OwnerFieldsDto ownerFieldsDto` — `OwnersApi.java:86`. The interface type is `@Validated` (`OwnersApi.java:44`). Because the `@Valid` sits on the interface method that the controller overrides, Spring validates the body **before** the controller body executes.

## 2 & 3. Request body DTO and its Bean Validation annotations

The request body is `OwnerFieldsDto` (there is no separate entity-bound DTO; the JPA `Owner` entity is not the request body). Generated at `/home/daniel/sandbox/target/generated-sources/openapi/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/dto/OwnerFieldsDto.java`. Validation annotations sit on the getters (enforced by `@Valid`):

- `firstName` — `OwnerFieldsDto.java:62`
  `@NotNull @Pattern(regexp = "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$") @Size(min = 1, max = 30)`
- `lastName` — `:83`
  `@NotNull @Pattern(regexp = "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$") @Size(min = 1, max = 30)`
- `address` — `:104`
  `@NotNull @Pattern(regexp = "^.*\\S.*$") @Size(min = 1, max = 255)`
- `city` — `:125`
  `@NotNull @Pattern(regexp = "^.*\\S.*$") @Size(min = 1, max = 80)`
- `telephone` — `:146`
  `@NotNull @Pattern(regexp = "^[0-9]*$") @Size(min = 1, max = 20)`

No validation groups are used. If any of these fail, the flow short-circuits into `MethodArgumentNotValidException` handling (see section 6).

## The Owner entity (persisted object, not the request body)

- `telephone` (`:46-50`): `@NotEmpty @Digits(fraction = 0, integer = 10) @Pattern(regexp = "^[0-9]{10}$", message = "Phone number must be exactly 10 digits")`
- `pets` (`:52-53`): `@OneToMany(cascade = CascadeType.ALL, mappedBy = "owner", fetch = FetchType.EAGER)`
